sentences.text: This genus includes only one species, Patagosuchus anielensis, which is recognized by its highly varied teeth.
Its mouth featured small, serrated front teeth followed by large, laterally compressed caniniform teeth behind them.
The animal also possessed unusually wide gaps between its teeth, a trait unique among peirosaurids.
The name Patagosuchus blends 'Patagonia' with 'suchus', the Greek word for the Egyptian crocodile god.
Knowledge of this creature comes solely from the holotype specimen MANE-PV 1, a single individual.
This fossil was found at the Baal Quarry, located twelve kilometers south of Añelo City in Neuquén Province.
Lio, Agnolína, Juarez Valieri, Filippi, and Rosales first named the species anielensis in 2015.
Patagosuchus belongs to the family Peirosauridae.
It lived between 93.9 and 85.7 million years ago during the late Turonian to early Coniacian stages.
